newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tsang hints govt may hold off property curbs.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tsang hints govt may hold off property curbs.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang has indicated the government may hold off on steps to curb speculation in the residential property market, the Sunday Morning Post reported.

"The decision whether to do something would rest on whether the current situation affects the lives of ordinary people, that is, whether it affects middle or lower-priced property, which (is) what the public needs," the Post quoted Tsang as saying on Saturday.
There was no need to intervene now since speculation had not spread to the middle and lower end of the market, Tsang added.
However, Tsang said a package of measures to control speculation would be implemented when necessary, but did not give a timeframe, the newspaper reported.
Spiralling property prices, which rose by 20 percent to 30 percent in 1996 caused in part by speculative buying, have been a major focus of concern recently in the territory.

The issue prompted Governor Chris Patten to say last week that his administration was keeping the property market under urgent review, raising expectations that the government would soon act to stamp out speculative buying.
Punting has also been rife in the trading of buying rights in the black market, where leading places in the queue to purchase flats have traded up to HK$2 million recently.

Some private developers have also stepped in to try to limit speculative activity by reducing to 20 percent the units on sale to shell companies -- seen as the main culprits in inflating prices through trading of buying rights.
In Sun Hung Kai Properties' apartment sale in the New Territories on Saturday, a record 27,000 people applied for the 1,864 flats on offer.
Nearly all the units had been sold by nightfall, the Post reported.
